claims.claim: Krege's rendering of Sam's 'Master' as 'Chef' (boss) was criticised as misrepresenting a rural gardener's relation to his employer, and the September 2012 revision removed it.

Krege spanned registers from sixteenth-century Bible German to colloquial speech but anchored them to 1990s German rather than the 1940s of the original, and many readers rejected the differentiation as overdrawn.
Krege's 'unermüdlich wedelndem Laubwerk' for 'ever-moving leaves' was attacked for distorting the symbol of transience and Elvish departure.
The German film dubbing kept Carroux's version rather than Krege's, visible in the third film's title remaining 'Die Rückkehr des Königs'.
Krege aimed to reproduce Tolkien's speech registers from Biblical language to 1940s British colloquialism, against what he saw as Carroux's uniform, artificially folksy German.
Krege's 1998 Hobbit restored the poems Scherf had cut but interpreted sentences freely and admitted anachronisms such as 'Hurricane'.
Krege said he wanted to translate as Tolkien would write in 1999, directly from Westron into German.
Krege's slang such as 'Penner' (bum) and 'Dalli Dalli' (hurry up) dated quickly and read as anachronistic.
Krege replaced the historical deferential 'Ihr' with modern 'Sie', creating an odd modern formality in a medieval society.
Editor Ulrike Killer defended Krege's version as timely for the films and preferable to a monochromatic and dated Carroux.
Lisa Kuppler's 2012 revision preserved Krege's stylistic approach but corrected orthography and restored the traditional address for Frodo.

claims.feature: translator's theory of colour and tempo
claims.claim: Krege (Tolkien Times, August 2000) set out to give the text its own life in the German language's room for 'Farbe, Tempo, Kontrasten'.
claims.source: Anmerkungen zu den deutschen Übersetzungen des HdR (Frank Weinreich, polyoinos)

claims.claim: Krege argued the old faithful translation inevitably makes the expression a little paler, the tempo slower and the style more uniform; Weinreich rejects 'paler' as nonsense but grants the rest.
claims.source: Anmerkungen zu den deutschen Übersetzungen des HdR (Frank Weinreich, polyoinos)
claims.quote: ein wenig blasser, das Tempo langsamer

claims.claim: Weinreich argues 'Master' and 'Sir' express Sam's working-class standing against Frodo's gentry more than an employment relation, so Carroux's 'Herr' is correct and Krege's 'Chef' means what 'Boss' would mean, which is not in Tolkien.
claims.source: Anmerkungen zu den deutschen Übersetzungen des HdR (Frank Weinreich, polyoinos)
claims.quote: das steht bei Tolkien aber nicht

claims.claim: In the Aglarond sentence Carroux keeps Tolkien's 'make ... bend' construction at some cost to fluency, while Krege's 'Kräuter' for 'weed' is botanically wrong where 'Wasserpflanzen' is right.
claims.source: Anmerkungen zu den deutschen Übersetzungen des HdR (Frank Weinreich, polyoinos)
